questions.q: What does DefaultAzureCredential do in this script, and why does it matter for Chapter 7?
options: It tries multiple credential sources automatically — a signed-in CLI session on a laptop, or a pipeline's service principal in CI/CD — without the script storing a secret itself
It hardcodes a username and password directly in the Python script
It only works when the script is run manually, never inside a pipeline
It is a Python-only feature with no equivalent for pipelines
questions.explain: DefaultAzureCredential lets the same script run unchanged on a laptop or inside a CI/CD pipeline, because it picks up whichever credential source is actually available.

questions.q: Why does the compliance-checking script only report tag violations instead of automatically adding the missing tags?
options: Because silently guessing and inserting tag values would be worse than the problem — nobody would know which tags were real and which the script invented
Because Python cannot modify Azure resource tags
Because adding tags automatically is always faster and safer than reporting them
Because the script has no way to write any output at all
questions.explain: The lesson explains this is a deliberate scope choice: reporting violations for a human (or follow-up ticket) to fix is correct; silently fabricating tag values is not.

questions.q: What is the purpose of sys.exit(1 if violations else 0) at the end of the script?
options: It gives the script an exit code a CI/CD pipeline step can read, so the pipeline can treat a run with violations as a failed step
It deletes the violations.csv file if no violations were found
It restarts the script automatically if violations are found
It has no real effect — pipelines never check exit codes
questions.explain: A pipeline step reads an exit code, not printed text; a non-zero exit code is what lets the pipeline surface the failure or block a deployment.

questions.q: Why does the script write its findings to a CSV file instead of only printing them to the console?
options: A printed message disappears when the terminal closes, while a CSV file becomes a build artifact the pipeline keeps for whoever responds to a failure
CSV files run faster than printing to the console
Printing to the console is not supported in Python scripts run by a pipeline
A CSV file is required for DefaultAzureCredential to work
questions.explain: A file the pipeline retains as an artifact gives a human the exact list of offending resources, not just a number of violations.

questions.q: Which two tags does this script require on every resource in Thornfield Analytics' subscription?
options: CostCenter and Owner
AutoShutdown and Environment
Region and SKU
DoNotDelete and Tier
questions.explain: The script's REQUIRED_TAGS list checks for CostCenter (for chargeback) and Owner (for accountability) on every resource.
